subject: Reserved capacity commit proposal and GPU-index clause discussion
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: James Park <james.park@auroraai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity sizing + term proposal (AuroraAI)

Hi James —

Thanks again for the time on Thursday. Attached is a first-pass reserved capacity proposal that maps your expected Q3–Q4 traffic to a 12‑month committed pool. Main points: 1) initial reserved fleet of 80 A100-equivalent units (burst to 120 for 8 weeks), 2) 12‑month term with quarterly usage true‑ups, and 3) a GPU-index clause to protect both parties given current market volatility (we included an optional cap/floor).

Can you confirm AuroraAI’s preferred commit tenor (12 vs 18 months) and whether procurement needs an indexation construct tied to a public GPU price index? If you prefer, we can reduce fixed commit and add a volumetric buffer to handle launch spikes.

I’ll follow up with a short sensitivity workbook for finance.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: James Park <james.park@auroraai.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@auroraai.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity sizing + term proposal (AuroraAI)

Thanks Irene —

We reviewed the deck internally. Main ask from procurement: any fixed commitment needs a clear mechanism if GPU spot prices move >15% quarter-over-quarter. We’d like either: (A) a GPU indexation clause (public index or cloud VM price reference) with a +/- cap; or (B) a tiered discount ladder that automatically steps as unit price changes.

Also, AuroraAI prefers an 18‑month commitment if we can get stronger downside protection in year 2 (i.e., price floor for us, pricing tie-down for you). Can you share the sensitivity workbook you mentioned and internal note on discount approvals?

—James
VP of Platform, AuroraAI
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Reserved capacity sizing + term proposal (AuroraAI)

Karthik / Ben —

Looping you in on AuroraAI’s procurement ask. They want an 18‑month tenor but with a GPU-price protection mechanism. I’ve attached the sensitivity workbook (gpu_price_sensitivity.xlsx) showing three scenarios: baseline (flat GPU cost), downside (prices drop 20%), and shock (prices up 30%).

Options I’m considering to present back:
- Indexed clause: tie to public GPU index (monthly settlement), capped +/- 12% per quarter and annual true‑up.
- Tiered discount ladder: larger up‑front discount for higher committed units, with automatic step-down if our internal GPU procurement cost exceeds threshold.
- Hybrid: modest commit + optional burst pool that’s billed at a floating rate beyond the committed units.

We’ll likely need approval for >18% aggregate discount over list if we do year‑2 protection. Ben, can you run a quick margin hit at -20% GPU price vs +20% scenario and flag the upper approval threshold? Karthik, flag if we should escalate to pricing committee or keep within σ_allowance.

Thanks — Irene

Attachments: gpu_price_sensitivity.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Reserved capacity sizing + term proposal (AuroraAI)

Team —

Quick digest of the sensitivity workbook: with the proposed base price and 80-unit commit, our incremental gross margin stays >48% in baseline and downside (-20% GPU cost) scenarios. If GPU prices rise +30% and we keep fixed pricing through year 2, margin slides to ~18% — below our comfort band.

Recommendation:
1) Approve indexed clause with a quarterly settlement band of +/-12% and an annual reconciliation. That keeps upside for us while protecting Aurora from runaway prices.
2) Allow up to a 15% one-time discount from list (sales allowance) for committing to 18 months; anything beyond 15% needs pricing committee sign-off.

If Karthik agrees, I’ll draft the internal approval memo and simulate the P&L with a capped year‑2 protection (price floor at -10% relative to list).

—Ben
Head of Commercial Finance, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed commit & GPU-index approach (AuroraAI)

Hi James / Aurora procurement —

Appreciate the clarity on tenor. Based on internal review (attached sensitivity workbook), Redwood can support an 18‑month reserved commitment with the following construct: 

- Commit: 80 reserved A100-equivalent units; burst up to 120 (operationally subject to capacity windows).
- Pricing: fixed unit price for committed units with quarterly GPU-index reconciliation using public GPU spot index (settles quarterly). Indexation band: +/-12% per quarter. Any quarter that exceeds +/-12% will be reconciled at the capped band; annual reconciliation resets exposure (no retroactive credits if cumulative outside caps exceed thresholds).
- Protection cap: Redwood will provide a price floor to Aurora of -10% relative to list for year 2 but any price protection beyond 15% aggregate discount requires pricing committee approval.
- Approvals & next steps: we’ve attached the sensitivity workbook and a redline of the term sheet. If Aurora accepts, please confirm by EOD Friday and we’ll route a pricing committee memo for the >15% path if selected. We can also route the DocuSign envelope once legal is aligned.

Link to draft doc & deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/582934/deal/DEAL-2026-0587

Best regards,
Irene Choi
